items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) to test a new drug called ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd). The study compares I-DXd to standard chemotherapy to see if patients live longer overall and if their cancer takes longer to grow or spread. This is a novel antibody-drug conjugate targeting a different pathway than current treatments.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial: Tulmimetostat Combinations for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-phase trial is recruiting patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) to test tulmimetostat (an EZH2 inhibitor) in combination with darolutamide or abiraterone. The study will evaluate safety, tolerability, and how well these combinations work. This targets patients earlier in their disease course before they become castration-resistant.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial: Tulmimetostat Plus Luxdegalutamide for mCRPC
items.summary: This trial is recruiting patients with progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) to test the combination of tulmimetostat (an EZH2 inhibitor) with luxdegalutamide (a next-generation anti-androgen) versus standard care. The study will assess safety and effectiveness of this dual epigenetic and hormonal approach.

items.title: Phase 2 Trial: Intermittent Therapy for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Disease
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial evaluates intermittent treatment with relugolix plus an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer who have good PSA response. The goal is to determine if treatment breaks can maintain cancer control while potentially reducing side effects and improving quality of life.

items.title: Phase 2 Trial: SYNC-T Cell Therapy SV-102 for mCRPC
items.summary: This trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to test SYNC-T Therapy SV-102, a novel cell-based immunotherapy. The study will evaluate safety, tolerability, and effectiveness while identifying the optimal dose for future studies. This represents a new immunotherapy approach for advanced prostate cancer.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who haven't received prior hormonal agents or chemotherapy. It compares mevrometostat (an EZH2 inhibitor) combined with enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone to determine if the combination works better than standard treatment.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial: AZD9750 With or Without Saruparib
items.summary: The ANDROMEDA trial is recruiting patients with metastatic prostate cancer to test AZD9750, a first-in-human drug, alone or with saruparib (a PARP inhibitor). The study evaluates safety, how the body processes the drugs, and early evidence of effectiveness in this new treatment approach.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial: AMO959 With Lutetium-PSMA Plus ARPI
items.summary: This trial is recruiting patients with PSMA-positive mCRPC who failed one prior hormonal therapy. It tests AMO959 in combination with lutetium-177-PSMA radioligand therapy and an androgen pathway inhibitor. The goal is to determine safety and effectiveness of this triple combination approach using targeted radiation.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial: TIL Immunotherapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This first-in-human trial is recruiting patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and prostate cancer to test CC-38, a treatment using tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL). The study assesses the feasibility of this personalized immune cell therapy approach where a patient's own immune cells are expanded and reinfused.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial: Radium-223 With M3814 and Avelumab
items.summary: This trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to compare radium-223 alone, radium-223 plus M3814 (a DNA damage response inhibitor), or all three drugs plus avelumab immunotherapy. The study tests whether enhancing radiation effects with DNA repair blockade and immune activation improves outcomes.

items.title: Phase 1 Trial: 177Lu-PSMA-VG01 for PSMA-Positive mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial is recruiting patients with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to receive 177Lu-PSMA-VG01, a radioligand therapy. The study evaluates how the drug distributes in the body, radiation dosimetry, safety, and early anti-tumor activity of this PSMA-targeted radiation treatment.

items.title: Phase 2 Trial: Enzalutamide Plus Lu-PSMA-617 for mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 randomized trial (no longer recruiting) compares enzalutamide alone versus enzalutamide plus Lu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy in chemotherapy-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study investigates whether adding targeted radiation improves outcomes over hormonal therapy alone.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Enhanced Therapy Plus Targeted Radiation After Surgery
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial is recruiting patients whose prostate cancer returned after surgery (biochemical recurrence). It tests two approaches: adding apalutamide plus abiraterone to standard radiation and hormone therapy, and adding metastasis-directed radiation for patients with cancer spread detected on PET scans. This uses advanced imaging to guide personalized treatment.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial: GSK5471713 First-in-Human Study for mCRPC
items.summary: This first-in-human study is recruiting adults with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to test GSK5471713 as a single agent. The trial evaluates safety, tolerability, how the body processes the drug, pharmacodynamics, and early clinical activity to establish the benefit-risk profile of this novel therapy.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial: GSK5458514 Alone or Combined for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This study is recruiting prostate cancer patients to test GSK5458514 alone or with other anti-cancer agents. Conducted in two parts (dose escalation and expansion), it evaluates safety and how well the body handles this drug, aiming to identify optimal dosing for future studies.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Olaparib Plus Abiraterone First-Line for mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial (no longer recruiting) evaluates olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) plus abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone as first-line treatment for Chinese patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't received chemotherapy or newer hormonal agents. It assesses whether adding DNA repair inhibition improves outcomes.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone for Chemotherapy-Naive mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial is recruiting chemotherapy-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients to compare xaluritamig (a bispecific antibody) plus abiraterone versus investigator's choice of treatment. The primary goal is to determine if the combination improves overall survival compared to standard options.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Castration-Resistant Disease Through Transcriptional Reprogramming
items.summary: This research review describes how chronic inflammation, particularly through NFκB and IL-6/JAK/STAT3 pathways, reshapes prostate cancer at the molecular level to promote progression to castration-resistant disease. These inflammatory signals work with androgen receptor pathways to drive tumor survival, spread, and resistance to treatment. The findings suggest targeting inflammation alongside hormonal therapy may improve outcomes.

items.title: DNA Vaccine Targeting PSMA Enhances Response to Immunotherapy
items.summary: This study tested a next-generation nanoplasmid DNA vaccine targeting PSMA in prostate cancer models. The vaccine increased PSMA-specific immune responses and, when combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade, achieved tumor eradication and prevented lung metastasis. Results showed increased immune activation and reduced immunosuppressive cells, suggesting potential for metastatic disease treatment.

items.title: Phase 2 Trial Results: Olaparib Plus Radium-223 for Bone Metastases
items.source: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
items.summary: This multicenter Phase 2 randomized trial (COMRADE) compared olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) plus radium-223 versus radium-223 alone in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases. The published results evaluate whether combining DNA repair inhibition with targeted bone radiation improves outcomes in this difficult-to-treat population.

items.title: Rucaparib Drug Evaluation for BRCA-Mutated mCRPC
items.summary: This drug evaluation reviews rucaparib, a PARP inhibitor approved for treating metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer in patients with BRCA mutations. The review covers the drug's mechanism targeting DNA repair deficiencies, clinical trial data supporting its approval, and its role in precision medicine for patients with specific genetic mutations.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes c-MYC Resistance in Metastatic Disease
items.summary: Researchers developed a new drug that blocks both BRD4 and AKT proteins to overcome resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Many cancers develop resistance to AKT inhibitors by increasing c-MYC protein levels. This dual-action compound addresses both pathways simultaneously, showing promise in laboratory models for patients whose cancer has become treatment-resistant.

items.title: Patient Quality of Life With Radium-223 Plus or Minus Olaparib
items.summary: This study reports patient-reported outcomes (quality of life measures) from the trial combining radium-223 with or without olaparib in castration-resistant prostate cancer patients with bone metastases. Understanding how treatments affect patients' daily lives, symptoms, and well-being is critical for treatment decisions, especially when comparing combination versus single-agent therapy.

items.title: Meta-Analysis: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Disease
items.summary: This comprehensive analysis of 21 clinical trials involving 1,580 patients examined how well immune checkpoint inhibitors work in unselected metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. Results showed modest benefits overall, but combination therapy with checkpoint inhibitors plus other agents showed better survival and progression-free survival than single or dual immunotherapy alone.
